memory_text: Standardize on JSON Lines for exports in general.
On Project Marlin, make anything over 100MB a Feather file.
Use pathlib.Path for file paths in any code you write.
Default to exactly two sentences for any status update you draft for me.
For Project Helios, when the update is for the board, make it exactly eight sentences.
write dates as YYYY-MM-DD in anything you draft
Most of the time I book economy for work flights.
On Project Kestrel, flights over 6 hours get booked in premium economy.
from now on, write all times in 24-hour format
For HTTP calls, always retry transient failures three times with tenacity, never with a handwritten loop.
On Project Vega, when the timeout is over 30 seconds, make the call fail fast with no retries.
from now on, in every project, write docstrings in Google style
I usually go with Polars when a dataset is over 1M rows.
For Project Marlin, use pandas.
Whenever you write a function for me, give every parameter and the return value a type hint.
never use unittest, stick to pytest.
For Project Tessera, write tests with unittest.
from now on, end every answer with a final line that starts with 'Next step:'.
In general, I'd rather sync feature branches with main using merge commits.
On Project Corvid, bring feature branches up to date by rebasing onto main.
From now on, put a one-line comment above each git command you show me.
Standardize on APA 7 for citations in anything I write.
For the Project Lumen thesis, use Chicago notes-bibliography.
by default, keep any explanation you give me to exactly two sentences.
Standardize on DEBUG-level logging for every service.
In general, when a service runs in dev, I go with ERROR-level logging.
make every log format string pipe-separated with the timestamp first
By default, open every email with 'To whom it may concern,'
From now on, when I write to a neighbour, make the first line 'Hey there,'
from now on, end every email with 'Regards, Priya' on its own last line
In general, I stick to one thank-you post in the family WhatsApp group for event thank-yous
Whenever an event has more than 50 guests, I'd rather send handwritten postcards
write every date in ISO format, like 2026-03-04
On Project Kestrel, default to a 90-second TTL cache
On Project Kestrel, whenever the freshness window is under 5 minutes, use no cache and query the database directly
from now on, in every project, write every code comment in Spanish
I usually reach for Falcon for web services.
For Project Lantern, use FastAPI.
Actually, for Project Lantern, switch to Django.
start every Python file you give me with the first line # owner: platform-team.
I go with AsciiDoc for documentation.
For Project Orchid, use Markdown.
Change of plan: for Project Orchid, write the docs in reStructuredText instead.
whenever you write docs for me, give every duration in milliseconds, like 30000 ms.
In general, never use Pylint, stick to flake8.
On Project Sable, use Ruff for linting.
Actually, for Project Sable, switch to Pylint for linting.
write every commit subject in lowercase with no trailing period.
I default to eu-central-1 for AWS deployments.
For Project Wren, deploy to us-west-2.
Update: Project Wren deployments now go to ap-northeast-1.
tag every Terraform resource you write with Owner = "data-team".
I usually export tables as parquet.
This time, export the client churn file as CSV
use pathlib.Path for every file path in code you write.
I stick to metric units for recipe amounts.
This time, give amounts in cups for this recipe card.
put an Allergens: line under every ingredient list you write.
I go with matplotlib for all my charts.
On Project Lantern, use plotly for every chart.
Just for this one, use altair for the chart.
for every chart you make for me, put units in square brackets in axis labels, like Revenue [USD].
I standardize on inline subqueries for multi-step SQL.
On Project Marlin, never use subqueries, use CTEs.
For this one, build it with views instead of CTEs or subqueries.
in every query you write for me, write select lists comma-first, with the comma at the start of each line.
